And in the year 596,
596 of the Arabs [1199–1200 AD],
al-Malik al-Adil gathered his forces,
and entered the land of Egypt.
And al-Afdal heard and also gathered his forces,
and went out and encountered his uncle;
and he was broken and fled by night,
and entered Cairo.
And al-Adil came and encamped against Cairo,
and desired to wage war against it.
Then the grandees advised al-Malik al-Afdal to send and sue for peace,
because he did not have the strength of al-Adil.
And al-Afdal sent to al-Adil for peace,
and asked that Damascus be given to him instead of Egypt;
and al-Malik al-Adil was not willing.
And he further asked for Edessa and Harran,
and he was not inclined to this either.
And he asked for Mayperqat, Hani, and Jabaljur,
and al-Adil consented.
And they swore oaths to one another.
And al-Afdal departed and went to Salkhad,
and sent his men to take delivery of Mayperqat.
However, the son of al-Adil,
who was Najm al-Din Ayyub,
rebelled and did not surrender it.
And al-Afdal sent to al-Adil concerning this,
and al-Adil made excuses,
saying: "My son has truly rebelled against my command, and does not obey me."
And when al-Afdal realized
that this was a plot between him and his son,
he contained himself,
and did not send an envoy again in this matter.
And in that year died the Khwarazmshah Tekish, son of Alp Arslan, the lord of Khwarazm and of part of Khorasan, Rayy, and the rest of the mountainous regions.
And his son Qutb al-Din Muhammad arose in his place,
the one who was also called Ala al-Din after the name of his father.
And in that year died Qadi al-Fadil,
the Egyptian jurist,
the unique one of his time in Egypt.
And in the year 597
(597 of the Arabs) [1200–1201 AD], al-Adil abolished the proclamation of the youth al-Malik al-Mansur, the son of al-Malik al-Aziz.
And it was displeasing in the eyes of the grandees,
and they wrote to al-Malik al-Afdal in Salkhad,
and to his brother al-Malik al-Zahir in Aleppo.
And they said to them:
"Come, encamp against Damascus;
and when al-Malik al-Adil comes out against you for battle,
we will bind him and deliver him into your hands."
